content: [Unknown - PREPARED_REMARKS]: Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) Q4 2024 Earnings Conference Call July 30, 2024.

[Executives Present - PREPARED_REMARKS]: Satya Nadella - Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Amy Hood - Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Brett Iversen - Vice President of Investor Relations
[Analysts Present - PREPARED_REMARKS]: Keith Weiss - Morgan Stanley Brent Thill - Jefferies Mark Moerdler - Bernstein Research Karl Keirstead - UBS

[Operator - PREPARED_REMARKS]: Greetings, and welcome to the Microsoft Fiscal Year 2024 Fourth Quarter Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. A question-and-answer session will follow the formal presentation.

[Brett Iversen - PREPARED_REMARKS]: Good afternoon, and thank you for joining us today. On the call with me are Satya Nadella, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer; Amy Hood, Chief Financial Officer; and Alice Jolla, Chief Accounting Officer.

[Satya Nadella - PREPARED_REMARKS]: Thank you, Brett. We closed out our fiscal year with a strong quarter. Microsoft Cloud revenue surpassed $36.8 billion, up 21% year-over-year. As a company, we are committed to helping our customers apply our platforms and AI tools to drive business growth. Azure continued to take share. Our AI business alone exited the fiscal year at an annualized run rate of over $5 billion, driven by both training and inferencing workloads.

[Amy Hood - ANALYST_QA]: Thank you, Satya. In Q4, total company revenue was $64.7 billion, up 15% year-over-year in constant currency. Gross margin percentage was 70%, relatively unchanged year-over-year. Operating income increased 15% to $27.9 billion. Intelligent Cloud revenue was $28.5 billion, up 19% year-over-year. Azure and other cloud services revenue grew 29% and 30% in constant currency, including 8 percentage points of growth from AI services. Demand for Azure AI services continues to be higher than our available capacity. We experienced some capacity

[Amy Hood - ANALYST_QA]: from AI services. Demand for Azure AI services continues to be higher than our available capacity. We experienced some capacity constraints in external GPU clusters, which slightly moderated Azure growth in Q4. Capital expenditures, including finance leases, were $19.0 billion in Q4, driven by investments to support cloud demand and accelerate our AI infrastructure footprint. Roughly half of our cloud and AI infrastructure spend was for long-lived assets that will support monetization over the next 15 years and beyond, including

[Amy Hood - ANALYST_QA]: and AI infrastructure spend was for long-lived assets that will support monetization over the next 15 years and beyond, including land and datacenter leases. Guidance for Q1 Fiscal 2025: In Intelligent Cloud, we expect revenue of $28.6 billion to $28.9 billion, with Azure growth of 28% to 29% in constant currency. We expect Azure growth to accelerate in the second half of fiscal 2025 as our massive capital investments in datacenter capacity and AI chips come online.
[Amy Hood - ANALYST_QA]: half of fiscal 2025 as our massive capital investments in datacenter capacity and AI chips come online.
[Operator - ANALYST_QA]: Our first question comes from Keith Weiss with Morgan Stanley.

[Keith Weiss - ANALYST_QA]: Thank you for taking the question. Amy, on Azure growth: 29% growth in Q4, guidance for 28% to 29% in Q1, with acceleration in the second half. Can you unpack the constraint? Is it purely GPU silicon allocation, or are power, data center shell, and networking also gating factors?

[Amy Hood - ANALYST_QA]: Keith, thanks. The constraint in Q4 and heading into Q1 is primarily server availability and power infrastructure timing. Demand remains ahead of capacity. We saw strong demand across both frontier model training with OpenAI and enterprise inferencing. When new capacity is delivered, it is monetized immediately. As our supply comes online in the second half of fiscal 2025, we will be able to fulfill that backlog, which is why we expect Azure growth acceleration.

[Operator - PREPARED_REMARKS]: Good afternoon. My name is Kevin, and I will be your conference operator today. At this time, I would like to welcome everyone to NVIDIA's Second Quarter Fiscal 2025 Earnings Conference Call. All lines have been placed on mute to prevent any background noise. After the speakers' remarks, there will be a question-and-answer session.

[Stewart Stecker - PREPARED_REMARKS]: Thank you, Kevin. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to NVIDIA's conference call for the second quarter of fiscal 2025. With me today are Jensen Huang, NVIDIA's President and Chief Executive Officer; and Colette Kress, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. Today's call is being webcast on the NVIDIA Investor Relations website.

[Colette Kress - PREPARED_REMARKS]: Thanks, Stewart. Q2 was another record quarter. Revenue of $30.04 billion was up 15% sequentially and up 122% year-on-year, well above our outlook of $28.0 billion. Data Center revenue of $26.3 billion was up 16% sequentially and up 154% year-on-year, driven by strong demand for our Hopper architecture GPU computing platform for training and inferencing large language models, recommendation engines, and generative AI applications. Cloud service providers represented roughly 45% of our Data Center revenue, and more than 50% came

[Colette Kress - PREPARED_REMARKS]: and generative AI applications. Cloud service providers represented roughly 45% of our Data Center revenue, and more than 50% came from enterprise and consumer internet companies. Networking revenue was $3.7 billion, up 16% sequentially and up 114% year-on-year, driven by our Quantum-2 InfiniBand platform and our Spectrum-X Ethernet networking platform for AI. Moving to Gaming. Gaming revenue was $2.88 billion, up 9% sequentially and up 16% year-on-year, reflecting higher shipments of GeForce RTX 40 Series GPUs. Professional Visualization revenue was

[Colette Kress - PREPARED_REMARKS]: up 9% sequentially and up 16% year-on-year, reflecting higher shipments of GeForce RTX 40 Series GPUs. Professional Visualization revenue was $454 million, up 6% sequentially and up 20% year-on-year. Automotive revenue was $346 million, up 5% sequentially and up 37% year-on-year, driven by self-driving platforms. Gross margin for the quarter was 75.1% GAAP and 75.7% non-GAAP. GAAP operating expenses were $3.93 billion, and non-GAAP operating expenses were $2.79 billion. We returned $7.4 billion to shareholders in the form of share

[Colette Kress - PREPARED_REMARKS]: $3.93 billion, and non-GAAP operating expenses were $2.79 billion. We returned $7.4 billion to shareholders in the form of share repurchases and cash dividends. Our Board of Directors approved an additional $50 billion in share repurchase authorization. Let me now address Blackwell. We shipped customer samples of our Blackwell architecture in the second quarter. We incorporated a change to the Blackwell GPU mask to improve production yield. Blackwell production ramp is scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter and continue

[Colette Kress - PREPARED_REMARKS]: Blackwell GPU mask to improve production yield. Blackwell production ramp is scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter and continue into fiscal 2026. In the fourth quarter, we expect to ship several billion dollars of Blackwell revenue. Demand for Blackwell platforms is well ahead of supply, and we expect this to continue into next year. Hopper demand is strong, and shipments are expected to increase in the second half of fiscal 2025. Outlook for the third quarter of fiscal 2025:

[Colette Kress - PREPARED_REMARKS]: shipments are expected to increase in the second half of fiscal 2025. Outlook for the third quarter of fiscal 2025: Revenue is expected to be $32.5 billion, plus or minus 2%. GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins are expected to be 74.4% and 75.0%, respectively, plus or minus 50 basis points. For the full year, we expect gross margins to be in the mid-70% range. GAAP and non-GAAP operating expenses are expected to be approximately $4.3 billion and $3.0 billion, respectively.
[Colette Kress - PREPARED_REMARKS]: in the mid-70% range. GAAP and non-GAAP operating expenses are expected to be approximately $4.3 billion and $3.0 billion, respectively.

[Jensen Huang - ANALYST_QA]: Thanks, Colette. NVIDIA achieved record revenues as global data centers are in full throttle to modernize the entire computing stack with accelerated computing and generative AI. Blackwell samples are shipping to our partners and customers. Generative AI will revolutionize every industry.
[Operator - ANALYST_QA]: Your first question comes from the line of Toshiya Hari with Goldman Sachs.

[Toshiya Hari - ANALYST_QA]: Hi, thank you so much for taking the question. Jensen, I wanted to ask about Blackwell and Hopper dynamics. You mentioned the mask change to improve production yields on Blackwell. Could you provide more color on the nature of that change? And secondly, how should we think about Hopper demand sustaining while customers wait for Blackwell to ramp?

[Jensen Huang - ANALYST_QA]: Thanks, Toshiya. First, let's talk about the Blackwell mask change. The functionality of Blackwell was complete from the start. Blackwell has 7 different chips that make up the architecture: the Blackwell GPU, the Grace CPU, the ConnectX-7 NIC, the BlueField-3 DPU, NVLink switches, and our optical transceivers. We made a mask modification to the Blackwell silicon to improve yield. There were no functional changes necessary. As a result, we will begin production ramp in Q4. We shipped engineering samples worldwide

[Jensen Huang - ANALYST_QA]: were no functional changes necessary. As a result, we will begin production ramp in Q4. We shipped engineering samples worldwide in Q2 and will ship production units starting in Q4.

[Now on Hopper demand - ANALYST_QA]: Hopper demand is accelerating, not slowing down. Why? Because the race to train frontier models and deploy real-time inference is urgent. Companies that invest in compute now generate returns immediately. Customers cannot afford to pause for six months; every month of delayed compute means losing market leadership. Hopper supply is increasing, and we will ship more Hoppers in Q3 and Q4 than in Q1 and Q2.
[Operator - ANALYST_QA]: Your next question comes from the line of Vivek Arya with Bank of America Securities.

[Vivek Arya - ANALYST_QA]: Thanks for taking my question. Colette, regarding the gross margin trajectory: Q2 non-GAAP gross margin was 75.7%, and Q3 guidance is 75.0%. As Blackwell begins its ramp in Q4, should we anticipate gross margin dilution during the initial ramp phase before stabilizing in the mid-70s?

[Colette Kress - ANALYST_QA]: Vivek, thank you for the question. Yes, let me walk you through our gross margin profile. As we start ramping Blackwell in the fourth quarter, initial manufacturing yields and the introduction of complex new packaging technologies like CoWoS-L and liquid-cooled NVLink racks will initially carry slightly lower gross margins. We anticipate gross margins in Q4 to experience a moderate headwind, likely landing in the low-70% range during the first couple of quarters of ramp. However, as yields optimize and volume

[Colette Kress - ANALYST_QA]: likely landing in the low-70% range during the first couple of quarters of ramp. However, as yields optimize and volume ramps throughout fiscal 2026, we expect gross margins to rebound swiftly back to the mid-70% range. Our full-year gross margin expectation for fiscal 2025 remains firmly in the mid-70% range.
[Operator - ANALYST_QA]: Your next question comes from the line of Stacy Rasgon with Bernstein Research.

[Stacy Rasgon - ANALYST_QA]: Thanks guys. Colette, regarding the $50 billion share repurchase authorization: can you discuss your capital allocation philosophy? You generated massive free cash flow this quarter. Why buy back shares at current multiples rather than expanding M&A or fab investments?

[Colette Kress - ANALYST_QA]: Thanks, Stacy. Our capital allocation strategy is disciplined and focused. First and foremost, we fully fund our R&D and organic growth initiatives. We are investing aggressively in our roadmap across silicon, software, and systems architecture. Second, we evaluate strategic ecosystem investments and selective M&A where appropriate. However, given our cash generation and strong balance sheet, returning capital to shareholders via repurchases reflects our supreme confidence in our multi-year growth trajectory and sovereign AI expansion.

Data Center revenue reached $30.8 billion, up 17% sequentially and up 112% year-on-year, driven by demand for Hopper H100 and H200 computing platforms across cloud providers, sovereign AI nations, and enterprise hyperscalers. Spectrum-X Ethernet for AI is gaining tremendous momentum, with tier-1 CSPs adopting our 800 Gbps networking switches. Gaming revenue was $3.28 billion, up 14% sequentially and up 15% year-on-year. Professional Visualization revenue was $486 million, up 7% sequentially and up 17% year-on-year. Automotive revenue was $449 million, up 30%

[Colette Kress - PREPARED_REMARKS]: Professional Visualization revenue was $486 million, up 7% sequentially and up 17% year-on-year. Automotive revenue was $449 million, up 30% sequentially and up 72% year-on-year, driven by autonomous driving compute modules. Gross margin for the quarter was 74.6% GAAP and 75.1% non-GAAP. GAAP operating expenses were $4.29 billion, and non-GAAP operating expenses were $3.05 billion. Free cash flow was $16.8 billion. In the first nine months of the fiscal year, we returned $26.2 billion to shareholders through repurchases and dividends.
[Colette Kress - PREPARED_REMARKS]: billion. In the first nine months of the fiscal year, we returned $26.2 billion to shareholders through repurchases and dividends.

[Update on Blackwell - PREPARED_REMARKS]: Blackwell is now in full-scale production. We shipped 13,000 GPU samples to customers in the third quarter, including engineering racks to OpenAI, Microsoft, and Google. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025, we expect to ship several billion dollars of Blackwell systems. Blackwell demand is staggering, exceeding our supply for several quarters into fiscal 2026. Hopper demand remains very strong and continues to grow into the fourth quarter. Outlook for Q4 fiscal 2025: Revenue is expected to be $37.5 billion,

[Update on Blackwell - PREPARED_REMARKS]: and continues to grow into the fourth quarter. Outlook for Q4 fiscal 2025: Revenue is expected to be $37.5 billion, plus or minus 2%. GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins are expected to be 73.0% and 73.5%, respectively, plus or minus 50 basis points. The temporary gross margin reduction in Q4 reflects the initial ramp cost of Blackwell architecture systems, complex NVLink liquid-cooled racks, and early manufacturing yields. Full year gross margins are expected to be in the mid-70% range, rebounding

[Update on Blackwell - PREPARED_REMARKS]: NVLink liquid-cooled racks, and early manufacturing yields. Full year gross margins are expected to be in the mid-70% range, rebounding in fiscal 2026 as Blackwell yields mature.

[Jensen Huang - ANALYST_QA]: Thanks, Colette. The age of AI is in full steam, propelling a global shift to NVIDIA accelerated computing. Blackwell is in full production, delivering up to 30x faster inference performance compared to Hopper for trillion-parameter frontier foundation models.
[Operator - ANALYST_QA]: Your first question comes from the line of Vivek Arya with Bank of America Securities.

[Vivek Arya - ANALYST_QA]: Thanks for taking the question. Colette, following up on gross margins: you guided Q4 gross margin to 73.5% non-GAAP, down about 160 basis points sequentially due to Blackwell ramp. Can you quantify the trajectory throughout fiscal 2026? Does Q1 mark the bottom of the gross margin curve, or will dilution extend into Q2?

[Colette Kress - ANALYST_QA]: Vivek, happy to unpack this. As we discussed last quarter, Blackwell introduces groundbreaking new packaging, including CoWoS-L, extreme interconnect density, and full system liquid cooling. In Q4, as we transition from initial sample units to commercial production, we incur initial manufacturing scrap and ramp costs. We anticipate gross margins will hover around 73% in Q4 and into the first quarter of fiscal 2026. Once Blackwell reaches high-volume production maturity in Q2 and Q3 of fiscal 2026, we anticipate gross margins

[Colette Kress - ANALYST_QA]: of fiscal 2026. Once Blackwell reaches high-volume production maturity in Q2 and Q3 of fiscal 2026, we anticipate gross margins will bounce back into the mid-70s, normalizing around 75%. Overall, customer willingness to pay for Blackwell's unmatched total cost of ownership (TCO) remains remarkably high.
[Operator - ANALYST_QA]: Your next question comes from the line of Timothy Arcuri with UBS.

[Timothy Arcuri - ANALYST_QA]: Thanks a lot. Jensen, there have been supply chain reports regarding overheating issues in dense NVLink liquid-cooled Blackwell GB200 NVL72 server racks. Could you directly address these cooling and thermal rumors? Are thermal issues impacting your Q4 shipping milestones or delivery schedules?

[Jensen Huang - ANALYST_QA]: Tim, thank you for bringing this up directly. Let me be 100% unequivocal: Blackwell production and delivery schedules are on track. There is no delay. When you engineer a 120-kilowatt, liquid-cooled, 72-GPU computing rack with thousands of cold plates, high-pressure quick disconnects, and copper backplanes, precision plumbing engineering is essential. We have designed and qualified multiple cold-plate and manifold cooling solutions with our ODM partners like Foxconn, Quanta, and Wistron. Engineering systems at this scale is an iterative collaborative process,

[Jensen Huang - ANALYST_QA]: solutions with our ODM partners like Foxconn, Quanta, and Wistron. Engineering systems at this scale is an iterative collaborative process, but every single Blackwell customer delivery milestone for Q4 and Q1 is moving forward as planned.

ITEM 2. MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS

Segment and Revenue Highlights:
Compute & Networking revenue increased 115% in the third quarter of fiscal year 2025 compared to the third quarter of fiscal year 2024, primarily driven by strong demand for our NVIDIA HGX platform leveraging Hopper architecture GPUs (H100 and H200). Cloud service providers represented approximately half of our Data Center revenue during the quarter.

Liquidity and Capital Resources:
As of October 27, 2024, we had $38.5 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities, compared to $26.0 billion as of January 28, 2024. In the first nine months of fiscal year 2025, we generated $43.9 billion in cash flow from operating activities, compared to $15.8 billion in the prior year period. Free cash flow was $16.8 billion for the third quarter of fiscal year 2025.
